evidence: Initial rows use source inspection plus named Rust regressions. Round two adds optional paired C/Rust TCP execution, captured in behavioral-wire.json; each new finding identifies its evidence in behavioral-audit-round2.json. Verification claims apply only to the stated contract.

behaviors.behavior: Forced exit movement moves executor and retains cause
behaviors.note: Resolved: typed movement requests separate executor, moved object and cause. Forced and nested queued exits move the executor, retain cause and do not borrow descriptors; TCP failure/restart coverage.

behaviors.behavior: Exit action sequence
behaviors.note: Resolved: exit success/leave/appearance/drop/move/enter providers and events match C order, contexts and DARK suppression. Per-phase callback rollback and TCP multiple-session delivery. Original cause retention differs at C command entrypoints; see M05.

behaviors.behavior: Original cause retained in ordinary movement callbacks
behaviors.note: Approved retention of original causal identity: Rust exit/generic requests retain the command cause. C move_exit and native enter/leave pass NOTHING to movement, and move_exit passes the player as traversal-lock cause. C get/drop pass the executing player to generic movement. Provider ordering/identities are tested separately from this caller-level difference.
